data.title: Dental Practice and Surgery
data.summary: A realistic dental practice: two surgeries of chair, delivery unit, operating light, stools and ported cabinet runs, a sterilising room and model lab behind them, and a reception and waiting area, all laid out from modular floor, wall, partition and door bays.
data.description: Everything a developer needs to build a working dental practice, from the treatment room out to the front door. The surgery is the heart of it: a dental chair with an upholstered seat, leg rest, recline back and headrest, in two liveries and in a reclined treatment pose; a mobile delivery unit whose bracket arm carries a tray of handpieces over the patient; a floor standing operating light on a jointed arm; operator and nurse stools on castored bases; a pedestal spittoon with a rinse cup holder; a suction unit with a collection jar; a wall mounted intraoral x ray set on a scissor arm; a sensor tray; a monitor on a pole bracket; and a 1 m cabinet module with a three drawer bank, a hinged door and a grey worktop that tiles into a run of any length, with a sink and mixer variant that drops into any position in it. Set out on the worktop are an instrument tray with a mouth mirror, a tapered probe and college tweezers, an ultrasonic scaler, a curing light in its cradle, a glove and mask dispenser bracket, a yellow sharps bin and a pedal bin. Behind the surgery wall is the room that keeps it running: a bench top autoclave whose round door opens onto a real chamber recess, an instrument washer with a drop down door, an ultrasonic cleaning bath, a loaded sterile pouch rack, a glazed sterile store cabinet, and a model lab with its bench, trimmer motor, burner, articulator, plaster arches, impression trays and case boxes. The front of house is a reception desk with staff screens, linked waiting chair runs in two colours, low tables, a water cooler, a coat stand, a bead maze play corner, an appointment screen and a notice board. The building itself is modular: a 2 m clinical floor tile with welded seams, and a 2 m wall bay in three kinds, plain, glazed and with a hinged surgery door, all sharing the same ports so a run mixes them freely, plus coved skirting, ceiling light panels, wall hand gel and a low surface temperature radiator. What moves is rigid node transforms only: the chair back and its headrest, the light arm and head, the delivery, monitor and x ray arms, autoclave, cabinet, store and surgery doors, the washer door, drawers, bin and bath lids, stool seats and the lab trimmer spindle. What does not move is said in each description and it is always the same reason: hoses, suction lines, gas tubing and power cables are flexible and this library has no skinning; the foot control, the pedal bin push rod and the articulator hinge are multi bar linkages one node cannot carry; and there is no water, no flame and no person anywhere. All original CC0 geometry, with no manufacturer, brand or product name in the geometry or the text.
